anomaly_def.Name: Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite Definition: A simultaneous condition where on-disk data or index structures are physically corrupted while the underlying storage subsystem is also approaching or has reached its space limits, causing the database engine to contend with both structural inconsistency and space-allocation failures at the same time.

Combined Observable Phenomena: Administrators may see checksum or page-verification errors interleaved with "no space left" or "cannot extend datafile" messages. Index scans can intermittently miss rows, yet forced full-table scans may also fail when the engine cannot allocate new extents or spill areas. Crash-recovery or DBCC/ANALYZE utilities invoked to repair corruption may themselves abort due to insufficient free space for scratch areas, redo, or snapshot copies. Log archives can back up, freezing write activity, while corruption in the same datafiles magnifies the urgency because standard online rebuilds or CTAS operations cannot proceed. Overall, query performance becomes erratic, with sudden fallbacks, blocking, and engine-level retry storms that are difficult to attribute to either space or integrity issues in isolation.

Causal Interaction: Space exhaustion can exacerbate latent or emerging block and index corruption by interrupting in-flight writes, online rebuilds, and checkpoint cycles, leaving partially written pages that violate structural invariants. Conversely, corruption inflates space pressure: orphaned pages, endlessly cycling crash-recovery attempts, and repeated error logging consume additional disk space, accelerating capacity depletion. The two root causes therefore create a reinforcing loop—corruption drives space consumption, space scarcity hinders corrective maintenance—pushing the database into a degraded state that is harder to recover without immediate administrative intervention.

entry.official_definition: Controls how long STOP REPLICA waits before timing out.
entry.trigger_condition: A STOP REPLICA administrative operation waits longer than rpl_stop_replica_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The administrative replication stop operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when replication endpoints stop exchanging or applying data within the configured timeout window, causing the channel to be considered inactive.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver status, upstream and downstream connectivity, and whether lag or stalled apply is preventing timely progress.
